entry.title: Payroll localization considerations for companies operating in Pakistan
entry.content:
I’m interested in how companies handle payroll when operating in Pakistan, particularly when the organization needs to manage local payroll requirements alongside its wider HR or ERP environment.

One area I find interesting is the amount of local payroll information that needs to stay accurate. Salary calculations are only one part of the process. Employee tax deductions, attendance and overtime data, leave adjustments, statutory contributions, payroll records, and reporting requirements all need to flow correctly into the monthly payroll cycle.

For organizations using SAP HCM or another enterprise HR platform, how do you normally approach this localization? Do you keep the local payroll calculation inside the main HCM environment, integrate a local payroll solution, or use a combination of both?

I've also been looking at payroll software in Pakistan and came across Vertex HCM, which takes a more localized approach to HR and payroll management. It made me curious about how other SAP professionals compare a dedicated local payroll system with a broader enterprise HCM implementation.

For those who have worked on Pakistani payroll implementations, what would you consider the most important factors when evaluating the local payroll layer, especially around compliance, integrations, attendance data and reporting?

Would appreciate hearing from anyone who has handled Pakistan payroll localization in an SAP environment.

entry.title: Issue with Automatic GL Clearing in F.13 – Employee-Level Identification
entry.content:
Dear everyone

   I am now facing a problem with Automatic GL Clearing of GL accounts using F.13. I would like your suggestions on how to solve this problem.

Scenario:

We have payroll wage types such as:

- Housing Advance

- Housing Advance Deduction

both wage types were linked to vendor accounts via payroll account assignment. The symbolic accounts were linked to vendor accounts, such as *0002.

A vendor account is created for each employee after hiring.

For example:

Employee: 7085

Vendor: 7007085

Existing Process – Vendor Account

Suppose an employee receives a housing advance of SAR 2,000 on 10.09.2026.

After payroll posting the amount is posted to the employee's vendor account:

Account                     Amount             Debit/Credit 

Vendor 7007085      SAR 2,000          Debit 

This line item can be viewed in FBL1N. The corresponding vendor items can be cleared using F.13.

During the regular payroll the housing advance is deducted from the employee through IT0015.

The accounting entry would then be:

Account                     Amount              Debit/Credit 

Vendor 7007085      SAR 2,000           Credit 

Since both entries are posted to the vendor account they can be identified and cleared against each other.

New Requirement – Common GL Account

The business requirement has now changed of creating/posting to an employee‑specific vendor account the housing advance and deduction should be posted to a common expense/balance sheet GL account.

For example:

10206000 – Housing

The accounting entries would then be:

Account                               Amount              Debit/Credit 

10206000 – Housing        SAR 2,000           Debit

Housing Advance Deduction

Account                             Amount             Debit/Credit 

10206000 – Housing      SAR 2,000          Credit 

Both transactions are therefore posted to the same GL account.

The FI users can view these line items in FBL3N based on company code, GL account and posting date.

Problem

The challenge is that when the employee‑specific vendor account is removed we no longer have an employee identifier that makes it easy to match which debit and credit items belong to the employee.

For example:

GL 10206000

10.09.2026 Debit 2,000 → Employee 7085

30.09.2026 Credit 2,000 → Employee 7085

15.09.2026 Debit 3,000 → Employee 7090

30.09.2026 Credit 3,000 → Employee 7090

From the GL perspective all these entries are posted to the account.

The customer wants to use Automatic GL Clearing to clear the debit and credit items preferably through F.13 while still being able to identify the employee behind each payroll posting.

What we have already checked

1. We checked whether PERNR is available in FBL3N. Could be used as the clearing criterion. However, PERNR is currently blank, for these GL line items.

2. We considered implementing a custom enhancement to populate PERNR in the FI line item/FBL3N. However, the FI users do not want PERNR to be displayed in their FBL3N report.

Therefore, we are looking for an approach where the employee can still be technically identified for Automatic GL Clearing purposes without displaying PERNR to FI users.

Questions

Has anyone faced a scenario where multiple employees payroll transactions are posted to the same GL account and the corresponding debit/credit items need to be automatically cleared?

What would be the recommended approach?

entry.title: Se excede tope de seguridad social en adelanto de vacaciones
entry.content:
El caso es el siguiente:

  • La empleada tiene 14 días de vacaciones: 9 en septiembre y 5 en octubre.
  • El adelanto de vacaciones se paga en septiembre por los 14 días completos.
  • Por esos 14 días, el tope proporcional es $2.189.482,62.
  • Luego, en la liquidación de septiembre, quedan 16 días para completar el mes (30 - 14).
  • Por esos 16 días, el tope que corresponde aplicar es $2.502.265,85.

Entonces:

$2.189.482,62 + $2.502.265,85 = $4.691.748,47

Esto coincide exactamente con el tope legal mensual de septiembre, por lo que es correcto.

El problema aparece si en septiembre se toman los 21 días de la liquidación para calcular el tope:

$2.189.482,62 + $3.284.223,67 = $5.473.706,29

Eso supera el tope legal mensual, por lo que es incorrecto.

Entiendo que el igualmente se ajusta una parte en octubre por eso 5 dias, pero entiendo que es incorrecto que supere el tope en septiembre.

Como podria solucionarlo ?

entry.title: Does SAP offer any AI-based tool for optimizing or debugging HCM time evaluation schemas and PCRs?
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

I’m an SAP HCM consultant working with Time Management, and I’m also doing an M.Sc. research project on whether LLMs and AI agents can help improve domain-specific configuration languages.

My case study is the Time Evaluation schema language. That means the schemas, sub-schemas and PCRs processed by RPTIME00. In our system, the main custom schema is about 1,300 lines with around 40 sub-schemas. As in most long-running implementations, it has built up over many years, so it’s hard to maintain, test and debug.

My question is: is there an SAP solution, current or on the roadmap, that uses AI to work with Time Evaluation schemas and PCRs? For example:

  • Analyzing a schema to find redundant, unreachable or conflicting rules
  • Suggesting simplifications or refactoring of PCRs
  • Explaining what a schema or rule does in plain language
  • Helping debug the time evaluation log, for example tracing why a given time type or wage type was or wasn’t generated

To be clear, I’m asking about schema and PCR configuration, not ABAP code. I know Joule and the Custom Code Migration agent support ABAP, but as far as I can tell they don’t cover Time Evaluation configuration.

I’d also like to hear:

  1. Has anyone tried using general-purpose LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) for schema or PCR work, and how did it go?
  2. Are there partner or third-party tools in this space?
  3. Is there someone at SAP working on HCM or Time Management who might be interested in research in this area?

Thanks in advance for any pointers or experiences.

Guy
